items.headline: Tech-led Rally Drives Markets Higher Amid Strong Earnings and Fed Focus
items.summary: U.S. equities closed higher today, spearheaded by robust performances in the technology sector following blockbuster earnings reports from key AI and software companies. Despite ongoing inflation concerns and the commencement of the Jackson Hole Symposium, positive corporate results fueled investor optimism. The market experienced a 'V-shaped' reversal, recovering from earlier declines to finish in positive territory.

items.headline: Okta Surges on Strong Q2 Earnings
items.summary: Cloud-based software company Okta saw its shares jump significantly after reporting strong second-quarter earnings that surpassed Wall Street expectations and raising its full-year guidance.

items.headline: Salesforce Soars on Earnings Beat, AI Partnership
items.summary: Salesforce surged following an impressive second-quarter earnings beat and the announcement of an expanded partnership with AI lab Anthropic.

items.headline: Veeva Systems Gains on Strong Fiscal Q2
items.summary: Veeva Systems experienced a significant gain after the specialized software company reported strong fiscal second-quarter 2027 results and elevated its full-year guidance.

items.headline: Nvidia Jumps on Blockbuster Earnings and AI Demand
items.summary: AI chipmaker Nvidia climbed higher after delivering stronger-than-expected profit and revenue for the latest quarter and providing robust forecasts, signaling continued accelerating demand for AI projects.

items.headline: Build-A-Bear Workshop Plunges on Weak Guidance
items.summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop shares fell sharply due to weak guidance for the upcoming period, despite reporting an earnings beat.

items.headline: Moderna Weakens
items.summary: Moderna shares were among the weakest performers today.

items.headline: Jackson Hole Symposium Kicks Off Amid Inflation Warnings
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's annual Jackson Hole Economic Symposium began today, with investors keenly awaiting clues on monetary policy. Two Fed officials expressed ongoing concerns about the persistent U.S. inflation outlook, emphasizing that the current rate of 3.4% remains above the central bank’s 2% target. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is scheduled to deliver a closely watched speech tomorrow.

items.headline: Technology and Non-Durable Consumer Sectors Lead; Energy and Healthcare Lag
items.summary: Today's market saw the Technology and Non-Durable Consumer sectors leading the gains, largely propelled by strong corporate earnings, particularly in AI and software. Conversely, the Energy sector lagged due to falling international oil prices, while Healthcare and Consumer Discretionary also experienced weaker performance.

items.headline: Key Economic Data Released: GDP and Durable Goods
items.summary: New economic data showed that the U.S. GDP grew at an annualized rate of 1.5% in the second quarter, remaining unchanged from initial estimates. Additionally, U.S. durable goods orders rose 1.1% in July, exceeding analysts' expectations. The Census Bureau also released new data products from its Business Trends and Outlook Survey.

items.headline: Earnings Season Continues Strong with Best Buy and Dollar General
items.summary: Beyond the tech giants, Best Buy ($BBY) reported better-than-expected Q2 FY27 results with comparable sales increasing by 4.1% and raised its full-year guidance. Dollar General ($DG) also lifted its outlook, reporting higher profit and sales.
